title: A finite algebra over a Nagata ring is Nagata
statement: Let $R$ be a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings making $S$ a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $S$ is a Nagata ring: $S$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ the domain $S/\mathfrak q$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. In particular, for every ideal $I\subseteq R$ the quotient ring $R/I$ is a Nagata ring.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032T (lemma-quasi-finite-over-nagata, line 45703), in the case of a finite ring map named there ('quasi-finite ring map (for example finite)'); the quotient R -> R/I is finite, generated by 1

proof.text: Fix a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ and let $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. The ring $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], since $R$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. The induced map $A:=R/\mathfrak p\to B:=S/\mathfrak q$ is injective: an element of $R$ maps to zero in $B$ exactly when it lies in $\mathfrak p$. Both $A$ and $B$ are domains. If $s_1,\dots,s_n$ generate $S$ as an $R$-module, their images generate $B$ as an $A$-module: every class in $B$ has a representative $\sum_i\varphi(r_i)s_i$, and reducing its coefficients modulo $\mathfrak p$ gives the claimed expression. Thus $A\subseteq B$ is a finite extension of domains [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], since it is generated as an $R$-module by $1$; it is N-2 by [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032T (lemma-quasi-finite-over-nagata), proof, lines 45708-45717; finite case

proof.text: Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$. The localization $K\otimes_A B=(A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}B$ is a nonzero domain and is finite-dimensional over $K$: the images of the same $s_i$ span it. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] it is a field. It contains $B$, so it contains inverses of every nonzero element of $B$ and is therefore $L$. Thus $L/K$ is a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. For any finite field extension $M/L$, the tower law [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] makes $M/K$ finite.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese), proof, lines 45206-45208 and finite case, lines 45224-45231

proof.text: Let $T_A$ and $T_B$ be the integral closures of $A$ and $B$ in $M$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Since $A$ is N-2 and $M/K$ is finite, $T_A$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. As $B$ is finite over $A$, every $b\in B$ is integral over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. If $x\in T_B$, then $x$ is integral over $B$, hence over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive]; therefore $T_B\subseteq T_A$. Conversely, a monic polynomial over $A$ vanishing at $x\in T_A$ is also monic over $B$, so $T_A\subseteq T_B$. Hence $T_A=T_B$. The finite set of $A$-module generators of $T_A$ also generates $T_B$ over $B$, because $A\subseteq B\subseteq T_B$. Since $M/L$ was arbitrary, $B=S/\mathfrak q$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Every prime $\mathfrak q$ has this property and $S$ is Noetherian by step 1; hence $S$ is Nagata [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese), finite case of proof, lines 45224-45231; used in Lemma Tag 032T (lemma-quasi-finite-over-nagata)

proof.text: For an ideal $I\subseteq R$, the quotient map $R\to R/I$ is finite: $1+I$ generates $R/I$ as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Applying the result just proved to this map shows that $R/I$ is Nagata.

split_report.summary: Split the finite case of Stacks 032T by writing out the finite-domain proof of 032I. For every prime quotient S/q, the contracted quotient A=R/p is an N-2 Noetherian domain and B=S/q is finite over A. Its fraction field L is finite over Frac(A); for each finite M/L the integral closures of A and B in M agree because B/A is integral. N-2 makes this common closure finite over A, hence over B. The quotient R/I is generated by 1 and follows as a special case. Reused only existing Mathlib leaves and definitions; no new node was needed.
